answer: Because the pulse lockup is enforced by the river escrow, the ivory audit can verify the release date and an early withdrawal attempt is rejected. The bond is locked for 35 epochs and cannot be withdrawn or transferred, so capital committed to an alias is unavailable for the whole term. Running a large swarm as a result freezes capital at scale for the full period, which is a cost that honest participants burn once per identity. That is 23 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
